report_name: CISA warns of XSS flaw in Johnson Controls Metasys ICS (CVE-2026-34491)

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-34491
vulnerabilities.description: A high-severity persistent (stored) cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability in the Johnson Controls Metasys building automation system UI. The flaw allows a low-privilege, authenticated attacker to inject a malicious script, which then executes in the browser of any user viewing the component, potentially leading to session hijacking and unauthorized control.

identities.name: Johnson Controls
identities.description: Vendor of the Metasys building automation system affected by CVE-2026-34491.

identities.name: CISA
identities.description: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which issued an advisory for CVE-2026-34491.

identities.name: Users of Johnson Controls Metasys
identities.description: Asset owners of the Johnson Controls Metasys platform, which is deployed globally in critical infrastructure sectors and is affected by CVE-2026-34491.

indicators.name: Potential Johnson Controls Metasys XSS Attempt
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Johnson Controls Metasys XSS Attempt
id: 2b1a9c8d-4e5f-4a3b-8c7d-6e5f4a3b2c1d
status: experimental
description: Detects potential Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attempts against Johnson Controls Metasys UI, indicated by script tags or JavaScript event handlers in URL requests.
references:
  - https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-225-14
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-14
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri|contains:
      - '<script>'
      - 'onerror='
      - 'onload='
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate URLs containing these strings in parameters for other applications.
level: medium
indicators.description: This indicator detects web requests containing common XSS payloads, such as `<script>` tags or `onerror` event handlers, which could indicate an attempt to exploit CVE-2026-34491 against the Johnson Controls Metasys UI.
